Thursday 6 February 2025 at 6.30pm

In accordance with section 5.27 of the Act, the Annual Electors Meeting will be held on Thursday 6 February 2025 at 6.30pm to receive the City of Albany Annual Report 2023-2024 and other General Business at the City of Albany Council Chambers, 102 North Road, Albany.

A copy of the annual report can be downloaded from the City’s website: www.albany.wa.gov.au.

Ordinary Council Meeting - 28 April 2020

Tuesday, April 28, 2020 - 6:00 PM

City of Albany Ordinary and Special Council Meetings commence at 6.00pm.

In response to advice regarding COVID-19, please be advised that until further notice, all Ordinary Council Meetings, Special Council Meetings and Council Committee Meetings will take place via the Zoom Video Conferencing platform.  

Members of the public that wish to join these meetings online (through Zoom) must register prior to the day of the meeting using this link: 

https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_QlV1wWe5Qx6jR3LbrfYQNg 

We appreciate your patience and understanding while we adapt to this new way of servicing our community. Please check our website for any updates to meeting dates and times https://www.albany.wa.gov.au/council-meetings/

Asking Questions

The City of Albany Standing Orders Local Law 2014 (Amended) provides an opportunity for the public to ask questions or address Council at Ordinary Council Meetings.  To ensure an equal and fair opportunity is provided to everyone wishing to address Council, a maximum period of four minutes per speaker is allocated.

Members of the public that wish to ask Council a question must submit their question via email to [email protected]  prior to the day of the meeting. Questions asked during Public Question Time without prior notice may need to be taken on notice if a response cannot be provided at the time of the meeting.

To Register for Public Question Time

  • Answer ‘yes’ to the “Do you wish to address Council?” when you register for the meeting using this link: https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_QlV1wWe5Qx6jR3LbrfYQNg 
  • Join the meeting using Zoom where you’ll be able hear and see the meeting but your microphone will be ’muted’.
  • During Public Question Time you will be ‘unmuted’ and asked to commence your address to Council.
  • At the end of your address you will be ‘muted’ again.
  • Once Public Question Time has been declared Closed by the Mayor, members of the public can take no further part in the meeting. You are welcome to continue as an observer/listener to the remainder of the meeting.

Using Zoom

Agendas & Minutes

Public Attendance

For community groups that wish to address Council on a matter concerning them, we may be unable to accommodate large groups in the Chambers. Please contact Council Liaison 6820 3076 to confirm the number of attendees prior to the meeting.

Should you wish to provide a written submission to Council regarding a matter on the agenda instead of attending in person, you may lodge it in writing, either by email to [email protected] or by posting to PO Box 484 ALBANY WA 6331. If mailing, please ensure that you allow adequate time for your submission to reach us by the day prior to the meeting.

For further enquiries please contact Council Liaison 6820 3076 or email [email protected]

Special Electors' Meetings

The Local Government Reform Bill 2023 passed through Parliament on 11 May 2023 delivering tranche one of the proposed local government reforms.

Changes to Special Electors' Meetings

The number of signatures required to call a Special Electors' Meeting has increased from 100 to 300.

The Mayor will have discretion to direct that a Special Electors' Meeting not be held regarding the same subject more than once in a twelve month period. If a refusal is made a report to the next Ordinary Council Meeting must be prepared explaining the refusal.

Standardised Meeting Procedures

Currently, Special Electors' Meetings are conducted in accordance with the City of Albany Standing Orders Local Law 2014 (as amended).

As part of local government reform, standardised meeting procedures will simplify how local government meetings are conducted, and provide uniformity across all local governments. 

The standardised meeting procedures will also apply to Special Electors' Meetings.

Further information regarding the reforms can be found here: Local Government Reform
